stem: A child with diabetes has suspected ketosis during a viral illness; which insulin approach is recommended for sick-day management?

options.text: Frequent extra doses of short-acting insulin
Withhold all insulin until ketones resolve
Use only the usual long-acting insulin
Stop short-acting insulin when oral intake is reduced
Delay any insulin change until the next outpatient appointment

explanation: Frequent extra doses of short-acting insulin are recommended for suspected or confirmed ketosis during sick-day management.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diabetes Sick Day Management

rationale: Frequent extra short-acting insulin is the recommended response to suspected or confirmed ketosis, rather than withholding insulin or waiting for routine review.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because suspected or confirmed ketosis requires frequent extra doses of short-acting insulin as part of active sick-day management.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because insulin should not be withheld when ketosis is suspected or confirmed.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because baseline long-acting insulin alone is not sufficient management for suspected ketosis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because short-acting insulin should not be stopped when oral intake is reduced if ketosis is suspected.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because insulin changes should be made promptly, not delayed until a routine outpatient appointment.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
